title: Internal-external attention switching SEEG epochs, DMN and DAN channels, 25 epilepsy patients (Hammer et al. 2024)
description: Stereo-EEG epochs from 25 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a task that required switching between external attention (visual search) and internal attention (answering questions about personal experiences). The derivative dataset contains the authors' preprocessed, bipolar-referenced epochs, spanning -4 to +4 s around each task switch. It includes only channels assigned to the default mode network (DMN) or dorsal attention network (DAN), together with MNI electrode coordinates. The data support analysis of low-frequency oscillatory dynamics and antagonistic network behavior during attention switching.
methods_description: SEEG was recorded with DIXI Medical depth electrodes and Quantum/NeuroWorks amplifiers at 2048 Hz, with reference and ground in white matter. The authors downsampled the data to 512 Hz and removed channels in the seizure-onset zone, irritative zone, or heterotopic cortex. They applied bipolar referencing, a 0.1 Hz high-pass filter and a 50 Hz notch filter with harmonics, and cut epochs from -4 to +4 s around each task switch. Contacts were localized on post-implantation CT coregistered to MRI and normalized to MNI space with SPM12. Channels were assigned to DMN or DAN with the Yeo-7 atlas.
